auth.approvals.gateA1: The proposer may not perform this — you would be performing it

auth.delegations.createHint: Delegations are granted through the API. A screen for granting one needs a person picker and a capability picker, and is deliberately not guessed at here.
auth.delegations.inForceHint: These are granting authority right now.
auth.delegations.intro: Authority one person lent another for a while. A delegation grants — it is the only thing here that does — so each one has an end date and a reason, and can be taken back at any time.
auth.delegations.noneActive: Nobody is acting under a delegation. Authority is being used only by the people who hold it themselves.
auth.delegations.nonePast: Nothing has expired or been revoked yet.
auth.delegations.pastHint: Kept deliberately. This is a record of what authority was lent, not only of what is in force.
auth.delegations.revoked: Revoked. It stops granting on the next request.
auth.denials.endedHint: Kept on purpose — this answers why somebody could not do something at the time, not only what is withheld today.
auth.denials.inForceHint: These permissions are being withheld right now.
auth.denials.intro: One permission taken from one person, without touching their role. A denial only ever subtracts — it can never grant anything — and it applies to everybody, including superadmins.
auth.denials.lifted: Given back. It applies again on the next request.
auth.denials.lockoutHint: A denial applies to superadmins too, so it is possible to withhold something from the only account that could give it back. The way out is on the server: mercato auth denials --tenant <id> --lift <denial-id>.
auth.denials.noneEnded: Nothing has been lifted or expired yet.
auth.denials.noneInForce: Nothing is withheld from anybody. Everyone can do what their roles allow.
auth.denials.permanent: Permanent — it will not lapse on its own

auth.projects.closedHint: Still governing. Closing a matter does not un-govern the records inside it — if anything the rules matter more afterwards, when nobody is watching it day to day.
auth.projects.grade.G0: Routine work with no effect outside the platform
auth.projects.grade.G2: Work that reaches customers or money
auth.projects.grade.G3: Work that is hard to undo, or that others depend on
auth.projects.grade.G4: Work with consequences the business cannot absorb
auth.projects.intro: The matters work is organised into. A project grades how consequential the work inside it is, and can narrow what its members may do there — it can never widen it, which is what makes it an overlay rather than a second set of permissions.
auth.projects.noneOpen: No open projects. Work is being governed by the ordinary rules — roles, policy and each record’s own state.
auth.projects.ungraded: Not graded — acts here stay at their ordinary level
auth.projects.writeHint: Projects are set up through the API. Creating one, adding somebody with a narrowed overlay and assigning records to it are three separate acts with three different consequences, and are deliberately not collapsed into one form here.

auth.trust.intro: How much room each worker has earned in one area of work, and why. Trust is a ceiling like everything else here — a high tier permits less supervision, it never permits an act that policy, the record or the invoker would refuse.
auth.trust.none: Nobody has been promoted yet. Every worker sits at the bottom tier, which means it may propose work but cannot carry any out on its own.
auth.trust.scaleHint: Each tier sets the most autonomy a worker may reach. Reads are exempt at every tier — a worker that may not read cannot do anything at all.
auth.trust.tier.T0: May propose work for somebody to carry out, and nothing more. Where every worker starts.
auth.trust.tier.T1: May act, but somebody approves each one before it takes effect.
auth.trust.tier.T2: May act, with the work reviewed after the fact rather than before.
auth.trust.tier.T3: May act on its own for most work, with the heavier classes still held back.
auth.trust.tier.T4: May act on its own up to whatever policy, the record and the invoker allow.
